doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Starting as an arranger; Frank Comstock
summary: Smith began as an arranger, studied from a Frank Skinner book, and talks about friend Frank Comstock and Jack Webb work.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you get into the big band scene? You played with Dorsey and Charlie Shavers.

I got into — I was 19 years old I think if I recall, yeah, 1941. Actually I started in the business basically as an arranger. The piano was a little bit secondary. I bought a book on arranging when I was a kid by Frank Skinner, and I had a band in high school, and another arranger, Frank Comstock was in the same harmony class I was in down there and he and I were friends. And he had a band too. I don’t know whether you’re familiar with Frank, but he did a whole lot of stuff for Les Brown when he was very young, and he did a lot of stuff for Jack Webb, which for some reason was kind of the kiss of death. You know when Webb died I mean everything just kind of turned off, and there’s no reason for it because this guy can really write beautifully.
Yeah. You know he did “Dragnet” and “Emergency” and—
I see. He was even in that movie, “Pete Kelly’s Blues.” Do you remember that? But getting back, you were a pretty self directed young man then.
